sources.title: Xbox Game Pass recebe Battlefield 6 e mais jogos esta semana! Veja os lançamentos (17)
sources.text: O Xbox Game Pass é um dos serviços de assinatura de games mais democráticos da atualidade, já que é possível acessá-lo de diferentes plataformas — incluindo os próprios, consoles da Microsoft, assim como no PC, nuvem, celulares, tablets e até Smart TVs Samsung e LG com modelos de 2022 para cá. Felizmente, seu catálogo também é atualizado quase que semanalmente, trazendo inúmeras opções para os assinantes aproveitarem — e o melhor de tudo: gastando pouco em comparação às novas tendências de preços da indústria. Se veio em busca de novos jogos para jogar através do Xbox Game Pass , está no lugar certo. O serviço ganhou um reforço de peso esta semana com a chegada de seis títulos para os assinantes aproveitarem. Confira abaixo mais informações sobre as novas aventuras! Battlefield 6 aposta em combates intensos, guerra em larga escala e destruição tática nos cenários. Assinantes do EA Play podem resgatar pacotes especiais e receber recompensas sazonais, enquanto usuários do Game Pass Ultimate também têm acesso ao serviço e a 10% de desconto em compras digitais elegíveis da EA. Desenvolvido no Brasil, Deep Dish Dungeon é um jogo de exploração e sobrevivência ambientado em uma masmorra artesanal repleta de quebra-cabeças. Com elementos de metroidvania e criação de itens, o título permite explorar suas profundezas sozinho ou em partidas cooperativas online. O jogo chegou em day one ao Xbox Game Pass. Dos criadores de Ghostrunner , Valor Mortis é um soulslike de ação em primeira pessoa ambientado em uma versão sobrenatural da era napoleônica. Na pele de um ex-soldado que retorna dos mortos, os jogadores enfrentam criaturas monstruosas, utilizam poderes especiais e investigam uma conspiração que ameaça a humanidade. O título também chegou em day one ao Xbox Game Pass. Em Bluey’s Happy Snaps , os jogadores exploram cenários conhecidos da série animada com Bluey e Bingo em uma aventura focada em fotografia. A experiência permite registrar momentos, descobrir animais da fauna australiana e jogar sozinho ou com uma segunda pessoa. Além disso, o jogo chegou em day one ao Xbox Game Pass. Chained Beasts , outro título day one do serviço, é um roguelike cooperativo para até quatro jogadores, que precisam enfrentar batalhas em arenas enquanto permanecem acorrentados uns aos outros. A mecânica permite usar as correntes e o próprio cenário para derrotar adversários, sobreviver a confrontos contra chefes e avançar pelos desafios. Por fim, em Beyond These Stars , que também chegou em day one no Game Pass, os jogadores constroem e administram uma cidade nas costas de uma baleia espacial enquanto viajam pelo universo. É necessário organizar cadeias de suprimentos, atender às necessidades dos habitantes, estabelecer postos avançados e interagir com espécies alienígenas para descobrir os mistérios do espaço. stories.title: Joguei o remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time e o clássico envelheceu bem
stories.summary: Após 90 minutos de demo, o remake chega ao Switch 2 em 5 de novembro com visual refeito, dublagem em português e ocarina que reconhece a voz. O post Joguei o remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time e o clássico envelheceu bem apareceu primeiro em Olhar Digital .

sources.name: Olhar Digital Games
sources.title: Joguei o remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time e o clássico envelheceu bem
sources.text: O remake de The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time chega ao Nintendo Switch 2 em 5 de novembro de 2026. Ele mantém a estrutura do clássico de 1998, mas muda o jeito de ver e de jogar. Joguei cerca de 90 minutos, e a primeira impressão é de um jogo que não parece velho nem desatualizado. Como estreante em Ocarina of Time, achei o desafio alto. Já joguei Zelda II: The Adventure of Link no NES, mas nunca Ocarina of Time. Por isso, este texto traz o olhar de quem chega sem nostalgia e evita spoilers, mesmo os que não surpreenderiam quem já jogou. As comparações com o original vêm de colegas que conhecem o jogo e testaram a mesma demonstração. O Olhar Digital foi convidado para jogar em primeira mão, e fui ao México viver esta experiência com outros influenciadores e pessoas da imprensa. Jogamos três partes diferentes, escolhidas para mostrar momentos, itens e mecânicas variadas. Primeiro veio o começo na Floresta Kokiri. Depois, uma exploração pelo Campo de Hyrule e pela Cidade do Castelo. Por fim, o Templo da Floresta, onde confesso que travei. Lançado originalmente para o Nintendo 64 em 1998, Ocarina of Time ganhou um primeiro remake no Nintendo 3DS, em 2011. O remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time é exclusivo do Switch 2 e aparece em um ano simbólico, o dos 40 anos da série. Na loja oficial da Nintendo do Brasil, o jogo custa R$ 329,90 na versão digital e ocupa cerca de 27 GB. Ele pode ser jogado no modo TV, semiportátil ou portátil, e já chega com texto e dublagem em português do Brasil. Quem já jogou outros exclusivos de lançamento da Nintendo, como Mario Kart World, sabe que o Switch 2 tem processamento de sobra. Em Zelda isso não mudou: a qualidade gráfica está linda. Segundo colegas que conhecem o original, os detalhes dos personagens estão fiéis ao jogo de 1998, com um toque a mais de modernidade. Joguei na TV, e as cutscenes são fluidas e encantadoras. O que mais me impressionou foi o conjunto: a arte gráfica, a dublagem em português e a trilha sonora trabalham juntas e transportam você para dentro do jogo. Em uma cena, a Grande Árvore Deko pede à Navi que procure o Link. Dá para sentir o peso da voz de Deko, a pressa da fada e o clima de expectativa. É meio que só assistindo mesmo para sentir, mas foi bem imersivo. Como já saiu um trailer com mais detalhes, dá para ver o cenário e as peças de roupa nítidos, rodando a 60 FPS. A Nintendo não divulgou números oficiais de resolução e taxa de quadros do jogo, e a página da loja no Brasil também não traz esses dados. Na TV, o que vi foi movimento e cenas fluidas. Os comandos de Link são simples: corrida, pulo e mira por giroscópio nas armas de projétil, como o estilingue. Quem conhece o original vai notar o botão de pulo, já que antes Link pulava sozinho nas bordas, e a câmera livre. As duas mudanças foram anunciadas pela Nintendo. O combate tem impacto sonoro e visual forte. Dá para pedir ajuda à Navi em várias situações, na qual ela explica os pontos fracos dos monstros, e colegas que conhecem o original disseram que ela está menos intrusiva do que no jogo de 1998. Esse recurso auxilia para não travar em certos momentos: não se esqueça de usá-lo! Joguei com pro controller, e não com Joy-Con, que, pelo que me disseram, também deve ser tranquilo. Na hora de trazer o review completo, conto como foi a experiência no modo portátil. A primeira parte foi o tutorial na Floresta Kokiri. Link precisa buscar os primeiros itens para encontrar a Grande Árvore Deko e iniciar a aventura, e Mido o impede de passar enquanto ele não tiver espada e escudo. Quem já conhece o jogo vai direto para os desafios. Por causa do tempo, fiquei com receio de explorar demais e perder as outras partes. Não conversei com todo mundo da vila e fui mais objetiva, até porque passei pelo tutorial para aprender os movimentos básicos. Depois da árvore, Link é enviado para sua aventura na floresta. Ali enfrentei as primeiras plantas carnívoras e, no meu caso, levei susto com aranhas gigantes que caem do teto da caverna. Há outros itens iniciais por lá, mas o mais importante foi encontrar o estilingue. Um aviso para quem tem aracnofobia, como eu: nessa fase há muitas aranhas. Não procurei nas opções para mudá-las, mas, como são fantasiosas, consegui me controlar. O Campo de Hyrule foi um momento de exploração, mas, por causa do tempo, fiz pouco. O campo é grande, e eu quis conhecer mais a Cidade do Castelo de Hyrule do que o campo em si. A cidade é linda, com pessoas interagindo, e os detalhes parecem de filme. Entrei em algumas lojinhas, mas me dediquei mais à missão da loja de insetos. A última parte foi o Templo da Floresta. Nessa dungeon há diversas salas, cada uma com um puzzle diferente para resolver, o que leva à parte seguinte. São quatro portas, e eu consegui resolver uma e meia, rs. A primeira é a mais simples. Depois, se você não acertar a ordem de resolução das coisas, isso te trava. Os puzzles são desafiadores e interessantes: envolvem mover blocos de área, acertar lugares estratégicos, coletar chaves pequenas e explorar corredores, como em um calabouço clássico. É por isso que digo que o jogo envelheceu bem e traz de volta o desafio dos jogos antigos. Na minha opinião, o desafio mais encantador é usar a ocarina. Você pode cantar para o console, murmurar ou até usar um instrumento para reproduzir a canção. O microfone do Switch 2 capta o som, identifica a melodia e reconhece a música, e Link a toca no jogo. Segundo a Nintendo, no remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time funcionam as canções que Link já aprendeu, e os botões continuam disponíveis. O recurso foi demonstrado pelo produtor Eiji Aonuma em um Nintendo Direct. No meu ponto de vista, ele deixa o jogo mais dinâmico. Muita gente tem dificuldade com ritmo no controle, e talvez cantarolar fique mais fácil. Também estão previstas para este ano ocarinas oficiais, incluindo um modelo elétrico da HORI. A dublagem em português ficou incrível: bem adaptada e acessível, e dá para perceber a preocupação da equipe da Nintendo com

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Zelda Ocarina of Time remake has new sidequests, harder minigames, and subtle dungeon tweaks
sources.text: Maybe there are a few surprises to be found after all I can't help but feel Nintendo is being a little too faithful with its upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake . I know I'm pretty isolated in that opinion, but with new info coming out of recent hands-on previews of the game, I've suddenly got reason to believe that Nintendo is looking out for my tastes, too. The Ocarina of Time remake will feature some new side quests, as demonstrated by longtime Zelda YouTube Zeltik . In Hyrule Castle Town, the guy at the potion shop will now be freaking out about a lurking bug when you first meet him, handing over an empty bottle for Link to catch it. Fulfill his request, and he'll let you keep the bottle and offer to fill it up with a healing red potion. This certainly isn't the kind of multi-stage side quest that you'd expect to have in a modern action-adventure game – and certainly, it doesn't seem that there's a journal or anything where you can track side missions – but it does suggest that Nintendo has designs on offering some things to do that'll be fresh even for those of us who've played through Ocarina of Time a dozen times over. There's also a new, harder version of the target shooting game where you have much less time to hit the targets, suggesting that we can expect some new challenge levels in the minigames, too. Zeltik's video also goes into depth on some minor, but meaningful, tweaks to the layout of the Forest Temple, suggesting that we won't be sleepwalking through the old dungeons, either. I was ten years old when I first played Ocarina of Time on N64, and it set me on a path to loving video games so much that they'd eventually become my job. I should be the perfect audience for the remake, but I've honestly been a little disappointed with how safe Nintendo seemed to be playing it. I know, I know, you can't mess too much with a stone-cold classic, but I already know Ocarina of Time forward and backward, and I'm afraid trundling through a remake offering little more than prettier graphics would ultimately feel a little empty. Offering a few little surprises around the edges, though? That suddenly makes the prospect of revisiting Hyrule a lot more exciting. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Hyrule feels more alive than ever thanks to clever expansion and a dose of Breath of the Wild vibes. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. sources.text: Publisher SEGA and developer RGG Studio have released the first in a set of multiple story trailers for each era of 50-year action adventure saga STRANGER THAN HEAVEN . The first is dubbed “Act 1: Kokura.” The description reads, “Trace the events that lead protagonist Makoto Daito to sneak aboard the trading merchant Orpheus’ ship bound for Japan, and the harsh realities that await in the first city he reaches: Kokura, Fukuoka.” STRANGER THAN HEAVEN is due out for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store on January 15, 2027. It will also be available via Game Pass.

sources.title: Rockstar leva carros de GTA 6 para as ruas de Miami antes do lançamento do game
sources.text: O Checkpoint desta sexta-feira (16) chega com novidades para o marketing agressivo do jogo mais aguardado de todos os tempos. A Rockstar levou versões reais dos carros de GTA 6 para as ruas de Miami — e os fãs estão pirando com os modelos nas redes sociais. Em outras notícias, Tyler Bahl, diretor de marketing da Activision, afirmou em entrevista ao The Game Business que Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 “encerrará este capítulo e dará início a um novo” para a série. Quer saber o que mais rolou no mundo dos games nesta sexta (16)? Então prepara o cafezinho da tarde e acompanhe o VOXL por mais um Checkpoint ! A Rockstar está levando carros inspirados em GTA 6 para as ruas de Miami, nos Estados Unidos, como parte da campanha de marketing do jogo. Os veículos foram modificados para lembrar modelos de Vice City, incluindo carros de polícia com placas da cidade fictícia, enquanto outras ações promocionais espalham a identidade visual da franquia pela região. A campanha também inclui um dirigível com a marca Vice City e aviões carregando banners promocionais. Embora as ações não mencionem diretamente GTA 6 , os vídeos dos carros circulando pela cidade já estão repercutindo nas redes sociais, com fãs empolgados com a iniciativa. O jogo tem lançamento previsto para 19 de novembro de 2026. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 marcará o encerramento da atual fase da série e abrirá caminho para uma nova direção da franquia, segundo Tyler Bahl, diretor de marketing da Activision. Em entrevista ao The Game Business , o executivo afirmou que o jogo será o “desfecho épico desta série recente de Modern Warfare ”. Bahl também destacou que a empresa pretende inovar nos próximos títulos para atender aos pedidos dos jogadores por experiências diferentes. “Estamos animados em encerrar este capítulo e iniciar um novo”, declarou. Segundo ele, o desafio será alcançar os diferentes públicos de Call of Duty , que possuem preferências variadas entre modos, personagens e subséries. Jeff Kaplan, ex-diretor de Overwatch , afirmou que não joga nem acompanha o shooter desde que deixou a Blizzard, em abril de 2021. Em entrevista ao GameSpot , o desenvolvedor explicou que se afastou completamente do jogo após 19 anos na empresa e adotou uma postura semelhante à que teve ao deixar World of Warcraft . Segundo Kaplan, a experiência anterior o ajudou a lidar melhor com a saída. “Eu tive um distanciamento quase clínico, sabendo como tinha sido a experiência com o WoW ”, declarou. O desenvolvedor também afirmou que entende que Overwatch agora pertence à equipe responsável pelo jogo, aos jogadores e à Blizzard, e não mais a ele. A Valve começou a disponibilizar os Conjuntos de Conquistas na Steam, recurso que permite aos desenvolvedores organizar as conquistas dos jogos em categorias separadas. A novidade está em fase beta com um grupo inicial de títulos e busca facilitar o acompanhamento do progresso, inclusive após a chegada de conteúdos adicionais. Cada conjunto terá uma barra de progresso própria e concederá um troféu de conclusão no perfil do jogador, que será preservado mesmo quando novas conquistas forem adicionadas. A Steam também permitirá arquivar conquistas e conjuntos, abrindo espaço para desafios sazonais e eventos por tempo limitado. Segundo a empresa, a funcionalidade ajuda jogadores que retornam a um título a identificar novidades sem perder o progresso anterior. Confira abaixo a lista de jogos que já recebeu o suporte — lembrando que mais títulos também receberão em breve: Ken Kutaragi, conhecido como o “pai do PlayStation”, afirmou compreender por que parte dos jogadores resiste ao abandono dos discos físicos. Em entrevista ao VGC , o ex-executivo da Sony reconheceu que a mídia física se tornou um símbolo de propriedade dos jogos, embora considere economicamente inviável manter esse modelo de distribuição. “Eu entendo que os discos físicos se tornaram uma metáfora para ‘possuir’ jogos. Eu realmente entendo essa mentalidade”, declarou Kutaragi. Ele também avaliou que a atual estratégia da PlayStation, cada vez mais voltada à conectividade e à distribuição digital, gera atritos com os fãs que valorizam os consoles e a posse tradicional dos jogos. sources.text: Horror RPG HorrorVale: Deadluxe Edition will launch for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , PlayStation 4 , Xbox One , and Switch on October 31, publisher Electric Airship and developer BatWorks Software announced. HorrorVale first launched for PC via Steam on October 1, 2024. Here is an overview of Deadluxe Edition , via Electric Airship: Welcome to HorrorVale! Your next-door neighbors are zombies, reanimated monsters deliver the mail, and ghosts hide out in your bathroom. Don’t worry about anybody you kill along the way—everyone is already dead! Muahahha! Bash monsters, recruit over 30 friends, and solve brain-buster puzzles! The year was 2016… Two best friends, one an artist and the other a musician, struck a deal. If the artist followed his dream to develop an RPG, the musician would provide the soundtrack. Over the years, many others were recruited to help, providing art, code and testing. What started as an idea between two friends was becoming something bigger than they had imagined. Finally, eight years and thousands of hours later, HorrorVale: Deadluxe Edition was complete. stories.title: ‘Father Of PlayStation’ Ken Kutaragi Blames A ‘Mentality Issue’ For The Backlash To Killing Discs
stories.summary: The Sony veteran doesn't sound very sentimental about the end of physical media on the platform he spearheaded

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: ‘Father Of PlayStation’ Ken Kutaragi Blames A ‘Mentality Issue’ For The Backlash To Killing Discs
sources.text: Ken Kutaragi practically willed the PlayStation into existence against the wishes and judgment of many others at Sony. His tenacity paid off. Decades after the PS1 launched, the PlayStation brand is dominant in the world of high-end console gaming. But the discs that propelled the platform to success are not long for this world, and Kutaragi thinks the death of physical PlayStation games makes sense. âI understand that physical discs have become a metaphor for âowningâ games. I really understand that mentality,” he told VGC in a new interview. “But nobody thinks [physical media] is necessary for a networked device like a smartphone, for example, because people feel that they will keep their content. So itâs a mentality.” He continued, âI really understand [why some people are upset], but I donât think itâs economically reasonable. Maybe itâs a mentality issue.” Despite Sony’s commitment to killing off discs in 2028, many die-hard PlayStation fans aren’t letting go without a fight . Part of that is nostalgia and sentimentality. Plucking discs out of cases and spinning them beneath lasers was an inseparable part of many people’s experiences with some of the most important games of the late ’90s and 2000s. But for others, it’s a matter of ownership rights and control. An all-digital future means Sony can do whatever it wants with your copy of a game, no matter how much you paid for it. One congressman is even proposing legislation to regulate the sale of digital games to make sure players own what they buy. While Kutaragi has been retired from PlayStation for almost two decades, he believes the writing is on the wall when it comes to a shift from hardware to cloud gaming, especially as the component cost crisis worsens.Â âIâm not the CEO at PlayStation anymore, but we still have some common [viewpoints]. Right now, Sony Interactive Entertainment has many people who have come from outside, like from Gaikai or streaming companies,” he told VGC .Â âSo itâs understandable that by utilizing network connectivity [they may see] PlayStation as not just a game console, but also a content terminal. Maybe thatâs how those people are thinking. But this has caused some friction with game enthusiasts.â Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. Legislative pressure could force companies to change how digital game licenses work The Power To The Players Act would put an end to digital game licenses The Legacy Games launcher is not long for this world Kaz Hirai was speaking in an interview about his management philosophy during his time heading the companyâs gaming push Game key cards have helped the company bridge the divide Support for PlayStation 3 discs appears to be on the way too

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: PlayStation creator backs Sony's call to end discs, says backlash is a "mentality issue"
sources.text: "I don’t think it’s economically reasonable" PlayStation's decision to end disc production for games in 2028 has unsurprisingly led to a massive amount of backlash, largely due to the implications an all-digital future holds for entitlements and actual ownership of a library of games. There have been notable voices in the industry expressing support, or at least trying to explain Sony 's stance amid ongoing component shortages and related hardware price pressures , and you can key PlayStation architect Ken Kutaragi among them. Kutaragi tells VGC at the Game Republic New Horizons event that he understands the pushback to Sony's decision, but ultimately sees it as a necessary step to navigate difficult economic headwinds. "I understand that physical discs have become a metaphor for 'owning' games. I really understand that mentality," he says. "But nobody thinks [physical media] is necessary for a networked device like a smartphone, for example, because people feel that they will keep their content. So it’s a mentality. "I really understand [why some people are upset], but I don’t think it’s economically reasonable. Maybe it’s a mentality issue." There's no doubt Sony and every other hardware manufacturer in business right now is under intense pressure to keep prices as low as possible despite an unprecedented economy squeezed by AI data centers and US tariffs, but many PlayStation users see the availability of physical discs as non-negotiable, leaving Sony and others in a real predicament going into the next console generation. Kutaragi has no direct insights into Sony's plans as he left the company in 2007, but he says he has an idea of the company's thinking in terms of hardware going forward. "I'm not the CEO at PlayStation anymore, but we still have some common [viewpoints]. Right now, Sony Interactive Entertainment has many people who have come from outside, like from Gaikai or streaming companies," says Kutaragi. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more "So it’s understandable that by utilizing network connectivity [they may see] PlayStation as not just a game console, but also a content terminal. Maybe that’s how those people are thinking. But this has caused some friction with game enthusiasts." I'd say "some friction" is an understatement , but it remains to be seen how Sony responds to what's become a public relations fire for the company. Some experts have suggested it's possible the conversation is evolving within Sony , but so far the company hasn't announced any plan to reverse course, nor has it shared additional details or assurances on how digital games will be handled going forward. Fans might not "pull out $1,000" for PS6 and Project Helix if all they can offer is marginal improvements, says ex-PlayStation boss After earning an English degree from ASU, I worked as a corporate copy editor while freelancing for places like SFX Magazine, Screen Rant, Game Revolution, and MMORPG on the side. I got my big break here in 2019 with a freelance news gig, and I was hired on as GamesRadar's west coast Staff Writer in 2021. That means I'm responsible for managing the site's western regional executive branch, AKA my home office, and writing about whatever horror game I'm too afraid to finish. stories.title: Samson Developer Liquid Swords Goes Bankrupt
stories.summary: Samson developer Liquid Swords is bankrupt after months of unpaid salaries, Breakit reports The post Samson Developer Liquid Swords Goes Bankrupt appeared first on Insider Gaming .

sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: Samson Developer Liquid Swords Goes Bankrupt
sources.text: Samson developer Liquid Swords is bankrupt after months of unpaid salaries, Breakit reports. Nearly 30 employees will receive state support. This was Liquid Swords’ first major release, which came out in April this year. A Breakit report from October 15 noted that the studio, founded by Christofer Sundberg, failed to pay employees for several months, and those affected will now receive state compensation. The report also noted that the bankruptcy trustee hopes to find a buyer. Founded by Christofer Sundberg, co-founder of Avalanche Studios and creative lead on Just Cause, Liquid Swords was their only released project. Samson had been in development since at least 2020 and drew inspiration from gritty open-world titles like Max Payne and Grand Theft Auto. Critics and players gave the game mixed reviews, with a 51 Metacritic score and a 5.2 user score on the platform. The game also has mixed reviews on Steam , with some players complaining about bugs and slow-to-respond controls. “This game has so many bugs, and the combat is very, very bad. It’s shocking that this game was released in 2026; this would make more sense if it were 2010, maybe. I waited for a few months to replay it again to give it a proper review, and I thought that it would be fixed, but nothing was fixed. Just not worth the time nor the money,” read one of the Steam Reviews. Other, more positive reviews glowingly praised the game’s atmosphere and its Steam Deck optimization. Still, as it stands, Liquid Swords faces impending bankruptcy, and Samson will be its only release. What are your thoughts on Liquid Swords’ inevitable bankruptcy? sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Liquid Swords, developer of open-city crime sim Samson, has gone bankrupt following staff claims that they haven't been paid in two months
sources.text: The administrator is currently seeking a buyer for the studio and its assets. Liquid Swords, the developer behind Samson , has gone bankrupt just six months after its run-based open-city crime sim was released. As reported by Breakit (via Rock, Paper, Shotgun ), a bankruptcy order was issued against the Swedish developer on October 12. According to Breakit, Liquid Swords' staff—around 30 employees—have gone unpaid for at least two months, and it was those employees who petitioned to have the company declared bankrupt. Liquid Swords was founded in 2020 by Christofer Sundberg, who previously co-founded Just Cause developer Avalanche Studios and co-directed that series' first game. Samson was Liquid Swords' debut title, an open city-crime sim with a distinctive run-based structure, where you play a getaway driver attempting to pay back an enormous mob debt by any means necessary. Samson was a difficult project for Sundberg and Liquid Swords. The studio initially intended for it to be a much larger action RPG. But the studio struggled to find a publisher for Samson, with one publisher rejecting Liquid Swords on five occasions. Last year, Liquid Swords ran into funding trouble, laying off half its team as a result. It also radically adjusted how Samson plays—which is how the run-based structure emerged. Upon its release in April this year, Samson received mixed reviews, with unfavourable (and somewhat unfair) comparisons to Grand Theft Auto being compounded by bugs and technical issues. In the months since, Liquid Swords has attempted to buff out Samson's various technical dents , releasing a patch as recently as October 8. Clearly though, that work hasn't produced a surge in interest in Samson, at least not enough to keep the lights on at Liquid Swords. What happens to Liquid Swords next is somewhat up in the air. The administrator for the studio—Cirio Law—has put the developer and its assets up for sale, including Samson itself, with the bidding window running open until October 21. As for the affected employees, the bankruptcy now means their unpaid salaries will be covered by the Swedish state wage guarantee . 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net . But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims. stories.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remaster rumoured, with leaker insisting it's not a remake
stories.summary: A remaster of cult 2004 RPG Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines may be in the works. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remaster rumoured, with leaker insisting it's not a remake
sources.text: A remaster of cult 2004 RPG Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines may be in the works. In a post on the r/GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit , a user wrote: "I can confirm that it is in the works. NOT a Remake, but a Remaster, with some caveats. That's all I can say". The poster says they have "previously leaked info on multiple other games", including that Forza Horizon 6 is set in Japan, but of course, all we can do is treat this as an unsubstantiated rumour for now. Their post follows an earlier thread about a possible Bloodlines remake, which they describe as having "kind of leaked" the news already. Separately, another post on the subreddit, flagged "Grain of Salt", links to a thread about the band Genitorturers, which was involved with the original soundtrack, mentioning a Bloodlines remake. ICYMI, Bloodlines 2 wrapped up development in June with its final post-launch update. The leaker also describes a "dire situation" in the games industry, saying they "expect many games that are in development right now to not see the light of day".

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Metal band Genitorturers allegedly claims a Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remake is coming, getting a dozen crusty nerds way too worked up
sources.text: This one is thin , man, but it has to do with one of my favorite games of all time , while the circumstances of the rumor are just kind of neat and weird, even if it turns out to be nothing. User Few_Interview8222 on the Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines subreddit reported back from a Genitorturers show in Brooklyn, New York. Partway through the set, the band supposedly told the crowd that a VtMB remake is happening. I haven't found any corroborating accounts of Few_Interview8222's story, but Genitorturers undeniably played at Brooklyn's The Meadows as part of their "Live + Lewd Tour" on October 15, which puts them in the right place at the right time. We've reached out to both rights-holder Activision (one of several, it's complicated) and Genitorturers' representation, and will update this story if we hear back. In addition to a killer score by Rik Schaffer , Bloodlines featured wonderfully era-appropriate licensed tracks from metal bands⁠—they were mostly used as diegetic music in the nightclubs and bars of Los Angeles. The Genitorturers track Lecher Bitch was the pitch-perfect theme of The Last Round, a downtown LA dive bar frequented by the Anarch faction of vampires. Multiple commenters on the Reddit thread point out that this could have been a confused, untimely, misinterpreted, or all of the above reference to last year's Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines 2 . You could easily imagine a concertgoer mishearing something in that context, or a performer fumbling delivery of the exact information. It's the sort of almost-but-not-quite thing you might expect from an artist with tangential awareness of a secondary fanbase they picked up over the years. A VtMB remake is also the sort of project you could see getting pingponged around between various actors and stakeholders: started, stopped, shopped around, etc. It'd be a situation ripe for collaborators on the periphery acting on outdated information. Rad! I think? It'd depend on who's doing it. More and more, I'm beginning to distrust anyone not named "Nightdive" when it comes to commercial remasters. See also: The recent Shogun 2 debacle and the fate of Deus Ex Remastered . Bloodlines is such a wild, janky, PC gaming package that Nightdive is the only studio I'd trust to not only do a remaster right, but also to bring on legendary modder Werner "Wesp5" Spahl, the man who's been keeping Bloodlines alive with one of the most impactful unofficial patch projects in gaming. A more ground-up remake would offer equally daunting challenges, like matching the one-of-a-kind mood and look Troika managed to evoke. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Bloodlines is one of my very favorite games and an incredible RPG that's well worth your time. To the uninitiated, I like to pitch it as an evolutionary missing link between 2D Fallout and New Vegas. Bloodlines boasts the open-ended design and reactivity of Fallout in 3D for the very first time (Bloodlines leads Leonard Boyarsky and Jason Anderson were senior talent on Fallout 1). Unlike New Vegas' wide open world, however, Bloodlines had a more linear, but still loose sequence of zones on a world map to explore. Bloodlines' Y2K, gothic, noir interpretation of Los Angeles is one of the coolest worlds ever presented in an RPG. A Nightdive treatment would be my preferred outcome: build on Wesp5's work and compensate him accordingly, then make it more accessible on more platforms at a modest markup over the original game. Bloodlines 1 can be had for $20 on Steam and GOG , but it's practically always on sale. Even if it turns out to be nothing, this is still just a neat, newsworthy little incident to behold—Genitorturers shouting out an obscure, beloved RPG like this 22 years later, and maybe getting a couple genre nerds like me a little too excited on the way. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Ted has been thinking about PC games and bothering anyone who would listen with his thoughts on them ever since he booted up his sister's copy of Neverwinter Nights on the family computer. He is obsessed with all things CRPG and CRPG-adjacent, but has also covered esports, modding, and rare game collecting. When he's not playing or writing about games, you can find Ted lifting weights on his back porch. You can follow Ted on Bluesky .
